title: Eddie Carl and the Carnes brothers
summary: Punch identifies Eddie Carl, trumpeter, and Eddie and Zinke Carnes, pianists, and the union president Arch Joe.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Well, who was Ed Carnes? Did you ever know Ed Carnes? Ed Carnes or Carnes or something like that?
Well, I know I played, Tramon played with Eddie Carl.

Well, he was on the, what do you know, he played on that show too. But I mean, I wasn't there when he played there, but I played with him with the Royal American show. Eddie Carl, trauma player, good old, good musician, man. He used to read, you sit down there and read the trumpet parts. Look over there and play the trumpet parts. Yeah. Eddie Carl, that was his name.
I just found a note about Al Wynn and Eddie Carnes. Carnes?
Carnes, Eddie Carnes. Oh, that's a piano player, Eddie Carnes. Yeah. Yeah, he was a piano player in Chicago.
Oh, yeah, Carnes, I know him good. He was a big time piano player.
Is that the same guy, they called Zinke?
Zinke Carnes and Eddie Carnes was brothers.
Oh, I see. Yeah. Who did Eddie work with? Eddie?

Well, he played with the man who got the union. What do you name him? Arch Joe. He played with him all the time. Arch Joe was a trumpet player too, but he's not, you know, he could read the music, but he never had no lip hardly. Arch Joe, he was the president of the union.
Did Al Wynn's work with Eddie Carnes? Yeah.

Well it was Carnes, Carnes outfits, you know, but they played all, what you call it, like Jeffrey Tavern, Chicago, big club there. This student there about, I'd say about six or seven years, this student had one spot, you know. They didn't play all around, there was another one spot.
